geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the monolithic stepped stack into a split-wing dominant mass to introduce a clearer public threshold while preserving a single governing form.
Orient the split to support a frontage-facing opening and maintain the long-bar neighborhood character.
Introduce a measured interstitial gap so the access edge reads as a real public seam rather than a sealed face.
Add a courtyard macro in the ancestry of the dominant mass to create a usable void tied to the ground plane.
Promote the courtyard wrapper to root so the hall/mass remains in ancestry while the new public void becomes governing geometry.
Set a substantial courtyard margin so the open-space figure is clearly legible in plan and section.
Align the court opening to the program access side to convert the frontage into active public ground.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the pure setback stack with a split-wing dominant mass to introduce a stronger public threshold while preserving the stepped overall gesture.
Align the split with the frontage direction so the opening reads toward the access edge rather than as a generic notch.
Open a measured seam to create a legible public void without destroying the dominant mass.
Add a courtyard wrapper in the ancestry of the mass so the frontage can become a usable ground-space figure.
Use a substantial margin so the void is clearly legible as public space rather than a minor subtraction.
Open the court toward the program access side to convert the street edge into an active threshold.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped compact mass that reads consistently across the four views, so it clears the basic visible-massing gate and has decent hierarchy and silhouette control. It also sits plausibly within the parcel in all views. However, the response is still essentially a sealed terraced block: the access edge is not meaningfully opened, and the public-space figure required by the neighborhood living brief is weak. The form therefore fits as an early massing placeholder for a mixed-use/neighborhood building, but only at a marginal level because the ground relationship is not yet articulated. The form is not so typologically wrong as to fail hard program fit, but it needs a carved court/notch or split to convert the frontage into a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this candidate; do not copy the vertical emphasis or assume a similar section is needed.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing with a clear dominant volume and setback logic can support a compact mixed-use presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology is materially different from neighborhood living; the candidate should not become a pure tower.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single coherent vertical profile can still read as one dominant mass if the section is continuous and legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is mostly a low horizontal commercial object; the candidate is more stacked and needs a more explicit ground void to match the brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low active ground condition and clear street-facing threshold strengthen neighborhood program fit.
